explanation: In right triangle ABC, tan B = AC/AB = 3/4, so the sides are in a 3-4-5 ratio. Since BC = 15, AC = 9 and AB = 12. Then BD = AB - DA = 12 - 4 = 8. DE is parallel to AC, so triangle BDE is similar to triangle BAC and DE/AC = BD/BA: DE = 9 · (8/12) = 6.
Similar figures have equal corresponding angles; only the side lengths are scaled. Angle P' corresponds to angle P, so it measures 30°. The scale factor 3 does not change any angle measures.

Let t = 7x - 250. Each of the eight angles is either t or 180 - t. A sum of four of them, using n angles equal to t, is n·t + (4 - n)(180 - t). For n = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 this gives -4t + 720, -2t + 540, 360, 2t + 180, and 4t, which in terms of x are -28x + 1,720, -14x + 1,040, 360, 14x - 320, and 28x - 1,000. Choices B, C, and D appear in this list, but -14x + 1,540 does not.
To convert degrees to radians, multiply by π/180. So 720 · (π/180) = 4π, which means a = 4.
The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. With a right angle and a 13° angle, a = 180 - 90 - 13 = 77. Choice D (103) would come from subtracting 77 from 180 again; it is not an angle of this triangle.
At the same time of day, height and shadow length are proportional: 555/300 = h/16. So h = 16 · 555/300 = 29.6 feet, which is closest to 30.

Let t = 9x - 140. The four angles are t, t, 180 - t, and 180 - t. A sum of two of them can be 2t = (18x - 280)°, 180°, or 2(180 - t) = 360 - 18x + 280 = (-18x + 640)°. So B, C, and D are all possible, but (-18x + 280)° is not.
In triangle ABC, angle ACB = 180 - 20 - 100 = 60°. Angle DCE is vertical to angle ACB, so it is also 60°. In triangle CDE, y = 180 - 60 - 40 = 80.
The area of a square is its side length squared, so the area is 35^2 square inches. Choice C, (4)(35), is the perimeter, not the area.
The side of length 21 is the hypotenuse (it is opposite the right angle). By the Pythagorean theorem, a^2 + 6^2 = 21^2, so a = sqrt(21^2 - 6^2). Choice B forgets to take the square root.
565π/6 = 94π + π/6. Since 94π is a whole number of full turns (47 · 2π), cos(565π/6) = cos(π/6) = (sqrt(3))/2.
The minor arc MN and the major arc MPN together make up the whole circle. So the circumference is 39 + 195 = 234 centimeters.
If A and B are the equal angles, B = 50°. If B and C are equal, B = (180 - 50)/2 = 65°. If A and C are equal, B = 180 - 50 - 50 = 80°. There is no case that gives 100°, so D is not possible.

Angle RTU is 114°, and since RT = TU, the base angles of triangle RTU are equal: each is (180 - 114)/2 = 33°, so angle U = 33°. In triangle SVU, the angle x° at V is an exterior angle, so it equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: x = 31 + 33 = 64.

Angles x and y are vertical angles, so 6k + 13 = 8k - 29, which gives k = 21 and x = 6(21) + 13 = 139. Angle z (above n, left of t) corresponds to the angle above m and left of t, which forms a straight line with x, so z = 180 - 139 = 41. Choice D (139) is the value of x, not z.

When every side is multiplied by 2, the area is multiplied by 2^2 = 4. So the area of PQRS is 4 · 5 = 20 square centimeters. Choice B doubles the area instead of multiplying by the square of the scale factor.
In an isosceles right (45-45-90) triangle, each leg is hypotenuse/sqrt(2) = 58/sqrt(2) = 29sqrt(2). The perimeter is 29sqrt(2) + 29sqrt(2) + 58 = 58 + 58sqrt(2).
OR and OS are both radii, so triangle ORS is isosceles and its base angles at R and S are equal. Each base angle is (180 - 88)/2 = 46°.
If every side is multiplied by 6, the area is multiplied by 6^2 = 36. So the area of EFGH is 36 · 54 = 1,944 square units. Choice C uses a factor of 6 instead of 36.
The angles of the triangle add to 180°, so x = 180 - 132 - 24 = 24. This matches the fact that PQ = QR makes the base angles at P and R equal.

Let the short side be s. The diagonal is 2s, so the other side is sqrt((2s)^2 - s^2) = s·sqrt(3). The area is s · s·sqrt(3) = s^2·sqrt(3) = 1,089sqrt(3), so s^2 = 1,089 and s = 33. The diagonal of an inscribed rectangle is a diameter of the circle, so the diameter is 2(33) = 66.

By the Pythagorean theorem, the other leg is sqrt(196.8^2 - 43.2^2) = sqrt((196.8 - 43.2)(196.8 + 43.2)) = sqrt(153.6 · 240) = sqrt(36,864) = 192. Choice D adds the squares, which would give a length longer than the hypotenuse.
In similar triangles, the perimeters have the same ratio as corresponding sides. Since DE = 2AB, the perimeter of DEF is 2 · 20 = 40. Choice C would be the ratio for areas, not perimeters.

Divide by 2: x^2 - 3x + y^2 + y = 22.5. Complete the square: (x - 1.5)^2 + (y + 0.5)^2 = 22.5 + 2.25 + 0.25 = 25. So the radius is sqrt(25) = 5. Forgetting to divide by 2 first leads to wrong values like those in C and D.
An equilateral triangle has three equal sides, so the perimeter is 3 · 28 = 84 inches.

Angle Y is the right angle. In right triangle XYR, angle X = 90 - a, so b = 90 - (90 - a) = a. Thus tan b° = tan a°. With sin a° = 12/13, the sides are in a 5-12-13 ratio, so cos a° = 5/13 and tan a° = 12/5. The length XY = 19 is not needed.

Surface area scales with the square of the edge length. If cube Y's edge is 3/88 of cube X's, its surface area is (3/88)^2 = 9/7,744 of cube X's, so n = 9/7744. Choice C uses the length ratio without squaring.
The angle x° (above p, left of t) and the 72° angle (below p, right of t) are vertical angles, so they are equal: x = 72. Choice C or D would come from treating them as supplementary or adding them.

The 175° angle at line h and the angle x° at line g are corresponding angles: both are below their parallel line and on the same side of line ℓ. Corresponding angles formed by parallel lines are equal, so x = 175.

fix.prompt: In the figure shown, line g is parallel to line h. Line ℓ intersects both lines. What is the value of x?

explanation: Each side is 852/3 = 284 cm. For an equilateral triangle, the circumradius is side/sqrt(3) = 284/sqrt(3) = (284/3)sqrt(3). So w = 284/3, or about 94.67.
Angle PRS is an exterior angle of triangle PQR, so it equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 163 = 132 + m∠QPR. So m∠QPR = 31°.

If each leg is L, the hypotenuse is L·sqrt(2), and the perimeter is 2L + L·sqrt(2) = L·sqrt(2)(sqrt(2) + 1). Since 94 + 94sqrt(2) = 94(1 + sqrt(2)), we need L·sqrt(2) = 94, so L = 94/sqrt(2) = 47sqrt(2). Choice C, 94, is the hypotenuse.

Since P, Q, R correspond to W, X, Y, the fourth vertices S and Z also correspond. Corresponding angles of similar figures are equal, so m∠Z = m∠S = 135°. The side lengths only affect the scale factor, not the angles.
TR = 584 is the longest side, so the right angle is at S. Angle W corresponds to angle T, so tan W = tan T = opposite/adjacent = RS/ST = 440/384 = 55/48. Choice C is tan R instead.
sin x° = opposite/hypotenuse. The side opposite the angle x° is 63 and the hypotenuse is 73, so sin x° = 63/73.
The two equal angles share 180 - 118 = 62°, so each is 62/2 = 31°. Choice C (62) forgets to split between the two angles.

Triangle ABC has base AC = 5 + 7 = 12 and height y, so its area is 6y. From 48 ≤ 6y ≤ 60, y is 8, 9, or 10. The small triangle is similar to triangle ABC, so x/5 = y/12 and x = 5y/12. That gives x = 10/3, 15/4, or 25/6; any of these is correct.

Increasing both the length and the width by 20% multiplies each by 1.2, so the area is multiplied by 1.2 · 1.2 = 1.44. The new area is 360 · 1.44 = 518.4 square inches. Adding just 20% to the area (432) is the common mistake.
The equation (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 has center (h, k). Here x - 1 means h = 1 and y + 7 = y - (-7) means k = -7, so the center is (1, -7).
A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has equation (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2. Here r = 7k, so r^2 = (7k)^2 = 49k^2. Choice A squares only the 7.
Area of a rectangle = length × width = 34 · 29 = 986 square centimeters.
Multiply radians by 180/π to get degrees: (9π/20) · (180/π) = 9 · 9 = 81 degrees.
The perimeter is the sum of the sides, so the third side is 18 - 4 - 6 = 8 centimeters.
Complete the square in x: x^2 + 58x + 841 + y^2 = 841, so (x + 29)^2 + y^2 = 841. The center is (-29, 0). Choice C has the sign of the x-coordinate wrong.
The volume of a cone is (1/3)πr^2h. So (1/3)πr^2(9) = (1/3)π, which gives 9r^2 = 1, r^2 = 1/9, and r = 1/3.
The angles of the triangle are 31°, 2b°, and a° = 45°, and they add to 180°. So 2b = 180 - 31 - 45 = 104 and b = 52. Choice D (104) is the value of 2b.
Multiply by 180/π: (16π/15) · (180/π) = 16 · 12 = 192 degrees.
In x^2 + (y - 6)^2 = 7, the right side 7 is r^2. Translating a circle does not change its radius, so circle B's equation also has a = 7. Then 4a = 28. The shift only changes h (to 96).

Angles B and G are already equal. Statement I or statement II gives a second pair of equal angles, so either one proves similarity by AA. Statement III gives FH = 3AC, but FH and AC are opposite the known angles, not the sides around them (that would require BC and GH). That is side-side-angle, which does not guarantee similarity.
The hypotenuse is sqrt(24^2 + 21^2) = sqrt(576 + 441) = sqrt(1,017). Since 1,017 = 9 · 113, sqrt(1,017) = 3sqrt(113), so d = 113.
TR = 52 is the longest side (20^2 + 48^2 = 52^2), so the right angle is at S. Angle W corresponds to angle T, so tan W = tan T = RS/ST = 20/48 = 5/12. Choice D, 12/5, is tan R.
Vertical angles are always equal, so angle 2 also measures 72°. Choice B (108°) would be the supplementary angle next to angle 1.
The two legs are both 15, so the triangle is an isosceles right triangle. Its two acute angles are equal and add to 90°, so x = 45.
The angle vertical to y° sits between the angles x° and z° on the same side of the horizontal line, so x + y + z = 180. Then z = 180 - 65 - 75 = 40.
Perimeter = 2(length + width) = 2(13 + 6) = 38. Choice B counts only the two lengths (2 · 13), and choice A only the two widths.

Angle S is a right angle, and W is on RT, so angles RSW and WST add up to 90°. For complementary angles, the cosine of one equals the sine of the other, so cos(∠RSW) = sin(∠WST) and the difference is 0, no matter where W is.
The 26° angle at line n is above ℓ and left of n. The angle corresponding to it at line m is above ℓ and left of m, which is supplementary to x° (above ℓ, right of m). So x = 180 - 26 = 154.
The hypotenuse is sqrt(28^2 + 20^2) = sqrt(784 + 400) = sqrt(1,184) = sqrt(16 · 74) = 4sqrt(74). Choice D forgets to take the square root.
The 64° angle at line k is above k and to the right of j. The angle corresponding to it at line ℓ is also 64°, and a° (above ℓ, to the left of j) forms a straight line with it. So a = 180 - 64 = 116.
The angles of a triangle add to 180°, so angle A = 180 - 52 - 17 = 111°.
The two diameters are perpendicular, so central angle AOC is 90°, which is 1/4 of the circle. The minor arc AC is 36/4 = 9.
Convert to degrees: 2π/3 = 120° and 5π/12 = 75°. Angle T is 120 + 75 = 195°. Choice B is angle R alone.

tan(A) = sqrt(3) means angle A = 60°, and angle D also equals 60° because it corresponds to A. In right triangle DEF with the right angle at F, DF is adjacent to D and DE is the hypotenuse, so cos 60° = DF/DE: 1/2 = 125/DE, so DE = 250.

fix.prompt: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF, where A corresponds to D and C corresponds to F. Angles C and F are right angles. If tan(A) = sqrt(3) and DF = 125, what is the length of DE?

explanation: All three side ratios equal 3, so the triangles are similar (SSS) with A ↔ D, B ↔ E, C ↔ F. Corresponding angles are equal, so angle EDF = angle BAC = 20°. The ratio 3 scales lengths, not angles.
Multiply degrees by π/180: 60 · π/180 = (1/3)π radians.
Circle A has center (0, 1). Shifting down 2 units moves the center to (0, -1), so the equation is x^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 49. Choice B shifts the circle up instead.
AB corresponds to QR and AD corresponds to QT. The scale factor is AB/QR = 12/5, so AD = (12/5) · 10 = 24 inches.
The area of a rectangle is length times width: 7 · 5 = 35 square centimeters. Choice B adds the sides instead.

Since PQ is parallel to XY and XY is perpendicular to YZ, angle PQZ = 90°. In triangle PQZ, angle QPZ = 180 - 90 - 63 = 27°. Angles XPQ and QPZ form a straight line along XZ, so angle XPQ = 180 - 27 = 153°.
92π/3 = 30π + 2π/3. Tangent repeats every π, so tan(92π/3) = tan(2π/3). The angle 2π/3 (120°) is in Quadrant II, where tangent is negative, and its reference angle is π/3, so the value is -sqrt(3).
Circle M has center (4, 5) and radius sqrt(9) = 3. Circle P has the same center and radius 6, so r^2 = 36: (x - 4)^2 + (y - 5)^2 = 36. Choice A doubles r^2 instead of r.

In triangle PQR, the right angle is at P (PQ is vertical, PR is horizontal) and both legs have length 2, so t = 45. In triangle LMN, the right angle is at L and both legs have length 2 + k, so it is also an isosceles right triangle and angle N = 45°. Since 45 = 90 - t, the answer is (90 - t)°.
Volume = Bh, so 216 = B · 8 and B = 216/8 = 27 cm^2.

Angles W and Y are both a°, and the angles at Q are vertical angles, so triangle WQX is similar to triangle YQZ with W ↔ Y, Q ↔ Q, X ↔ Z. The scale factor is YQ/WQ = 21/70 = 3/10, so YZ = (3/10) · WX = (3/10) · 60 = 18.
Angle BCA forms a straight line with the 110° angle, so it is 70°. Since angle BAC = angle BCA, angle BAC is also 70°. So x = 180 - 70 - 70 = 40.

GM = GN = 168 are radii, and the tangent segments MH and NH are equal: 2(168) + 2·MH = 3,856, so MH = 1,760. A tangent is perpendicular to the radius, so triangle GMH is right with GH as hypotenuse: GH = sqrt(168^2 + 1,760^2) = sqrt(3,125,824) = 1,768.
In right triangle ABC, angle C = 90 - 69 = 21°. Since the triangles are congruent with A ↔ D and B ↔ E, C corresponds to F, so angle F = 21°.
The radius is half the diameter: 12.6/2 = 6.3 centimeters.
